57	is *new* relative to AJC is the assembly and the class-transport, and those are

60	## The three gaps, kept apart
61	
62	`exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` is **single-field**: `k`, the cover `U₀, U₁` and
63	the base divisor `D₀` are all fixed.  It is therefore strictly weaker than the two
64	things downstream consumers eventually want, and neither is proved anywhere in
65	this project:
66	
67	* **extension uniformity** — the *same* `b` for every field extension `κ/k`.
68	  Needs flat base change of the bound along `k → κ`; nothing here quantifies over
69	  extensions, and note that even the *statement* needs the base-changed cover
70	  (`RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean` supplies `C_κ` as an AJC curve, but not the
71	  transported 2-affine cover data on which `Ȟ¹` here is pinned).
72	* **global generation** above the bound.  Needs `Ȟ¹(D − x) = 0` at every closed
73	  point `x`, i.e. the bound raised by the maximal residue degree, plus the
74	  evaluation-surjectivity argument.  Not addressed.
75	
76	`ajc-gate` should therefore not read this file as discharging a global-generation
77	or extension-uniform hypothesis; it discharges the single-field bounded-vanishing
78	shape only, and only relative to (1)–(3).

102	    Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D) ↔
103	      sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D ≤ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D := by
104	  constructor
105	  · intro hsub x hx
106	    have hzero : Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
107	        (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).subtype (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D))

109	    rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero, Submodule.mem_comap,
110	      Submodule.subtype_apply] at hzero
111	    exact hzero
112	  · intro hle
113	    constructor
114	    intro a b
115	    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ a
116	    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ b
117	    rw [Submodule.Quotient.eq, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply]

122	coboundary `B(D')`, with an overlap section of `𝒪(D)`.  Then `Ȟ¹(D')` vanishes.
123	
124	`D'` is typically `D + E` with `E ≥ 0`: this is "peel off an effective divisor",
125	the step that turns one base vanishing into vanishing on a whole cone.  The
126	`hpeel` hypothesis is the ledger's surjectivity datum `htwist`, unwound; it is
127	supplied here as a hypothesis because AJC has no unconditional source for it. -/
128	theorem subsingleton_h1Mod_peel {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
129	    (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D))
130	    (hpeel : ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D,
131	      x - y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D')
132	    (hle : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P ≤
133	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) :
134	    Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D') := by
135	  rw [subsingleton_h1Mod_iff] at hbase ⊢
136	  intro x hx
137	  obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := hpeel x hx
138	  have hyB : y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D' := by
139	    have : y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D := hbase hy
140	    exact coboundarySub_mono k U₀ U₁ hle this
141	  have : x = (x - y) + y := by abel
142	  rw [this]
143	  exact (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D').add_mem hxy hyB

146	modulo the coboundary `B(D')`, with an overlap section of `𝒪(D)`" — equivalently,
147	the twist `Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D')` is surjective.  Named so that it can be composed
148	(`Peel.trans`) and so that consumers can discharge it one point at a time rather
149	than in one step. -/
150	def Peel (D D' : X.WeilDivisor) : Prop :=
151	  ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D,
152	    x - y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D'

155	theorem Peel.refl (D : X.WeilDivisor) : Peel k U₀ U₁ D D :=
156	  fun x hx => ⟨x, hx, by simp⟩

158	/-- **The peel relation composes.**  `Peel D₀ D₁` and `Peel D₁ D₂` give
159	`Peel D₀ D₂`, provided `D₁ ≤ D₂` (so that `B(D₁) ⊆ B(D₂)`).

166	theorem Peel.trans {D₀ D₁ D₂ : X.WeilDivisor}
167	    (h₀₁ : Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D₁) (h₁₂ : Peel k U₀ U₁ D₁ D₂)
168	    (hle : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₁) P ≤
169	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₂) P) :
170	    Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D₂ := by
171	  intro x hx
172	  obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := h₁₂ x hx
173	  obtain ⟨z, hz, hyz⟩ := h₀₁ y hy
174	  refine ⟨z, hz, ?_⟩
175	  have : x - z = (x - y) + (y - z) := by abel
176	  rw [this]
177	  exact (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D₂).add_mem hxy
178	    (coboundarySub_mono k U₀ U₁ hle hyz)

181	`Peel E (1·P + E)` for every prime divisor `P` and every `E` — then `D₀` peels to
182	`divisorOfList L + D₀` for every list `L`, i.e. to `D₀` plus an arbitrary effective
183	divisor.  Induction on `L` with `Peel.trans`. -/
184	theorem Peel.of_list (hstep : ∀ (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (E : X.WeilDivisor),
185	      Peel k U₀ U₁ E (pointDivisor P + E))
186	    (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (L : List X.PrimeDivisor) :
187	    Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ (divisorOfList L + D₀) := by
188	  induction L with
189	  | nil =>
190	    have h0 : divisorOfList ([] : List X.PrimeDivisor) + D₀ = D₀ := by
191	      rw [divisorOfList, zero_add]
192	    rw [h0]
193	    exact Peel.refl k U₀ U₁ D₀
194	  | cons P L ih =>
195	    have hassoc : divisorOfList (P :: L) + D₀ =
196	        pointDivisor P + (divisorOfList L + D₀) := by
197	      rw [divisorOfList]; abel
198	    rw [hassoc]
199	    refine ih.trans k U₀ U₁ (hstep P (divisorOfList L + D₀)) fun Q => ?_
200	    exact le_add_pointDivisor (divisorOfList L + D₀) P Q

308	
309	The **closed ledger** is the identity `χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` for every Weil
310	divisor `D`.  In this project it is not a theorem: `chi_telescope_list` proves it
311	for *effective* divisors from a per-step hypothesis which is one application of
312	`chi_add_eq_residueDeg`, and that in turn consumes the ledger's
313	connecting/surjectivity data plus the strong-approximation input `hsurj`.  So the
314	statements below take the closed ledger as an explicit hypothesis, spelled
315	exactly as it will be discharged:
316	
317	`hledger : ∀ D, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D`.
318

320	here says "given the ledger, this follows", and the reader can see what is
321	missing. -/

327	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)

330	`chi_telescope_list` computes `χ(Σ_{P ∈ L} P)` as `χ(0) + Σ_{P ∈ L} deg P`, and
331	`degK_divisorOfList` computes `deg_k` of the same divisor as the same sum, so the
332	two agree: `χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` for `D = divisorOfList L`.
333

335	among several, and it shows the `hledger` hypothesis of this section is not

342	    (hbump : ∀ (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (E : X.WeilDivisor),

405	Given the closed ledger, this is a two-line consequence of the class-invariance of
406	`χ` proved in `ClassInvariance.lean`: `0 − div g` is in the class of `0`, so
407	`χ(0 − div g) = χ(0)`, and the ledger reads off
408	`deg_k (0 − div g) = 0`, i.e. `deg_k (div g) = 0`.

411	`principal_degree_zero`, which asserts the same for the unweighted degree
412	`Σ_P ord_P g`; see §4. -/

425	theorem degK_eq_of_linearEquivalence

442	one.**  `Σ_P ord_P(g) = 0` follows from the closed ledger together with
443	`[κ(P):k] = 1` on the support of `div g`.
444	
445	This makes the reduction of the open leaf `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`
446	machine-checked rather than merely asserted: the *whole* remaining content of that
447	leaf, given the ledger, is the residue-degree-one fact for a smooth proper curve
448	over an algebraically closed field.  It is stated here on the adelic hypotheses
449	(`Algebra k K(X)`, `IsConstantField`, a 2-affine cover, the ledger) rather than on
450	the leaf's own geometric hypotheses, which is why it does not literally close that
451	`sorry` — the missing step is instantiating these hypotheses from
452	`[IsProper] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1] [GeometricallyIrreducible]` over `k̄`,
453	together with `residueDeg k̄ P = 1`. -/
454	theorem degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one
455	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
456	    {g : X.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0)
457	    (h1 : ∀ P ∈ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from
458	      Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg).support, residueDeg k P = 1) :
459	    Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree (Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg) = 0 := by

466	
467	`degK_principal_eq_zero` above and the open leaf
468	`Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero` are **different statements**, and the
469	first does not imply the second.  Recorded here because the difference is easy to
470	misread as a formality.

472	* `degK_principal_eq_zero` concerns `deg_k (div g) = Σ_P ord_P(g)·[κ(P):k]`.  Its
473	  proof is the χ-transport of `ClassInvariance.lean` plus the closed ledger, and
474	  it is stated over an **arbitrary** base field of constants `k`.
475	* `principal_degree_zero` concerns the **unweighted** `Σ_P ord_P(g)`, and is
476	  stated on a smooth proper curve over an algebraically **closed** `k̄` with no
477	  field of constants in sight and no ledger hypothesis.
478	
479	Over `k̄` the two degrees coincide because every closed point of a smooth curve has
480	residue field `k̄`, i.e. `[κ(P):k̄] = 1`.  That collapse is
481	`degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one`, and composing it with
482	`degK_principal_eq_zero` gives `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one`:
483	the **unweighted** statement, proved, from the ledger plus residue-degree-one.
484	
485	So the reduction is now machine-checked, and the residue of the open leaf is
486	exactly two items, neither of them about divisor theory:
487	
488	1. `residueDeg k̄ P = 1` for every prime divisor `P` of a smooth proper curve over
489	   an algebraically closed `k̄` — a statement about residue fields of closed
490	   points (`κ(P)` is a finite extension of `k̄`, hence `k̄`);
491	2. the instance plumbing that places `principal_degree_zero`'s own geometric
492	   hypotheses in adelic shape: an `Algebra k̄ K(C)` with
493	   `IsConstantField k̄ C.left` (available — `Adelic/GateInstances.lean`), a
494	   2-affine cover, and the closed ledger for that cover.

497	with a call to `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one` would require
498	producing the ledger for a cover of `C`, and the ledger is itself not yet a
499	theorem here (see §3) — so the substitution would move the gap rather than close

1	# LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
2	
3	LeanAG Horizon is a multi-project Lean 4 and Mathlib workspace for formalizing algebraic
4	geometry with [Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon). Its central goal is
5	the algebraic-geometry version of the [Algebraic Jacobian challenge](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian.20challenge/near/587802685),
6	proposed by Christian Merten after Kevin Buzzard's differential-geometry challenge.
7	
8	> [!IMPORTANT]
9	> The workspace develops **two live routes** to the Algebraic Jacobian challenge. Follow the
10	> project named by the active task rather than treating either route as reference-only.
11	>
12	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` continues the ambitious Picard-scheme route, building
13	>   representability by the Milne–Kollár construction of `Pic^r`, then `Pic^0` and the Albanese
14	>   property. Its Grassmannian, graded-algebra and flattening-stratification substrate is sorry-free
15	>   and still consumed, but the Quot-scheme endgame it was first written for is not the path being
16	>   built.
17	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` develops a cleaner curve-specialized route
18	>   from protected target statements.
19	
20	The two projects share mathematical sources and supporting subprojects while keeping independent
21	Lean roots, blueprints, and roadmaps. The rebuild is listed first in the workspace manifest as the
22	default project; explicitly scoped tasks may and do advance the ambitious original route.
23	
24	The [live dashboard](https://axeldlv00.github.io/LeanAlgebraicGeometry/) is the best view of current
25	tasks, commits, session logs, blueprint graphs, and declaration-level progress. A static snapshot
26	is published approximately every 30 minutes; GitHub Pages deployment and caching can add a few
27	minutes before a new snapshot is visible.
28	
29	## Repository Layout
30	
31	| Path | Role |
32	| --- | --- |
33	| `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` | Cleaner curve-specialized AJC route and workspace default. |
34	| `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` | Ambitious Picard-scheme AJC route (Milne–Kollár representability), maintained by scoped tasks. |
35	| `SubProjects/` | Supporting, extracted, and related-paper formalizations available to the active project. |
36	| `references/` | Shared mathematical sources and retrieval notes. |
37	| `.archon-horizon/` | Workspace state: tasks, roadmap, inbox, run metadata, graphs, and ledger. |
38	| `config.yaml` | Ordered workspace manifest. The rebuild is listed first because it is the primary project. |
39	
40	Each route has its own overview:
41	
42	- [`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/README.md`](MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/README.md)
43	- [`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md`](MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md)
44	
45	## Project Map
46	
47	The workspace currently registers these projects, in priority order:
48	
49	| Project | Purpose |
50	| --- | --- |
51	| **`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`** | Cleaner curve-specialized route; default project in the workspace manifest. |
52	| `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` | Ambitious Picard-scheme, `Pic^0`, and Albanese route. |
53	| `Line-Bundle-Comparison-Iso` | Extracted line-bundle pullback, tensor, and dual comparison infrastructure. |
54	| `Albanese` | Albanese universal property, rigidity, and rational-map-extension infrastructure. |
55	| `Cech-Cohomology` | Čech computation of higher direct images and its cohomological substrate. |
56	| `GR-Quot-Closure` | Relative Grassmannian and quotient-representability infrastructure. |
57	| `MR0555258-Compactifying-Picard` | Compactifying the Picard scheme (D'Souza), under `SubProjects/RelatedPapersFormalisation/`. |
58	| `Picard-IdentityComponent` | Extracted Picard identity-component and `Pic^0` development. |
59	
60	These member projects remain useful sources of proved APIs, mathematical designs, and failure
61	memory for both main routes.
62	
63	## Working in a Main Project
64	
65	The workspace currently uses Lean and Mathlib `v4.31.0`. Build the project named by the task. For
66	the ambitious Picard-scheme route:
67	
68	```bash
69	cd MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
70	lake build
71	```
72	
73	The rebuild uses the shared workspace package directory at `.lake-packages`, so member projects
74	can reuse the same Mathlib checkout while retaining independent build directories.
75	
76	For workspace-wide exploration, run commands from the repository root:
77	
78	```bash
79	horizon dashboard
80	horizon graph -p Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge frontier
81	horizon search "Jacobian Picard representability"
82	```
83	
84	The first command starts the local dashboard. The graph command shows the ranked proof frontier
85	for the active project, and search queries declarations across the workspace and Mathlib.
86	
87	## Methodology
88	
89	[Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon) coordinates long-running
90	formalization while keeping mathematical and operational state explicit:
91	
92	- **Horizon sessions** implement and verify Lean proofs against concrete tasks.
93	- **Fresh-context reviewers** such as Ground, work-reviewer, and janitor are dispatched at review
94	  and maintenance checkpoints rather than acting as a permanent second driver.
95	- **Blueprint graphs (`hgraph`)** track declaration dependencies, proof status, comments, and the
96	  ranked frontier for each project.
97	- **Roadmap, tasks, and inbox** record strategy, scoped work, cross-session handoffs, and durable
98	  failure memory.
99	- **The workspace ledger** records coherent commits and powers the public dashboard's progress
100	  and session views.
101	
102	Concurrent sessions can share a project's root import file. When adding one
103	import, build the staged root from the ledger's current `HEAD` and insert only
104	that line; do not stage the whole on-disk root, which may contain another
105	session's uncommitted imports.
106	
107	The mathematical blueprint is kept separate from implementation journals. Lean-specific progress
108	and failed approaches belong in graph comments, tasks, or the inbox, while the blueprint remains a
109	timeless account of the mathematics.
110	
111	## Contributing
112	
113	Contributions are welcome, but keep the two routes and task scope explicit:
114	
115	- **AJC proofs and infrastructure:** change only the main project named by the task; share reusable
116	  inputs through the supporting projects when appropriate.
117	- **Protected statements:** do not alter the signatures in the rebuild's `Challenge.lean` or files
118	  covered by `archon-protected.yaml` without prior agreement. Contributions should discharge those
119	  statements, not weaken or reshape them silently.
120	- **Issues and discussions:** include the declaration name and file path, and state whether the
121	  question concerns the statement, naming, proof strategy, or intended use.
